main_text.l: catur teneritas cordis, & animæ puritas. 5 Peregri-
natio, quæ exitus è Mundo & itionis in occursum
futuri typus est, nec alio plerique eorum qui in ea
tationi hominis,an ea quæ ipsi mandata sint sectari
velit; quales sunt Cursus & Properatio in circuitio-
ne [(aabæ] & jactus lapillorum. Quod verò ad
sunt ea ad Congregationem populi, quo conveni-
ant, & se mutuò visant, & in iis à laborum tædiis
quiescant. Circumcisio autem injunctio est; cui in-
est tentatio & probatio, & deditio sui [Deo] Quod
ad prohibitionem Morticinii, & sanguinis, in eo
quod horreat ea animus,& refugiat natura, satis est
quod abstinentiam ab illis ut necessariam suadeat.

page.notes: Text begins mid-sentence ("depressio"), so the first paragraph is a continuation. Printed as "depressio" and "fubjugatio" with long s, rendered as plain s. The "5" before "Peregrinatio" is an inline section number in the text, not a heading. A small ink spot sits after "Peregri-" and another after "animus,", both stains, not printed marks. Spacing after "tendunt," and "animus," is irregular in print. The page has no catchword or signature.
